div.head: TRUE GRACE, DiſtinguiſhedDistinguished from the EXPERIENCE OF DEVILS.

epigraph.q: Thou believeſtbelievest that there is one GOD; thou doſtdost well; the Devils alſoalso believe and tremble.

div.p: OBSERVE in theſethese Words. 1. Something that ſomesome depended on, as an Evidence of their good EſtateEstate, and Acceptance, as the Objects of GOD'sGod's Favour, viz. a ſpeculativespeculative Faith, or Belief of the Doctrines of Religion. The great Doctrine of the ExiſtenceExistence of one only GOD is particularly mentioned; probably, becauſebecause this was a Doctrine wherein, eſpeciallyespecially, there was a viſiblevisible and noted DiſtinctionDistinction, between profeſſingprofessing ChriſtiansChristians and the Heathens, amongſtamongst whom the ChriſtiansChristians in thoſethose Days were diſperſeddispersed: And therefore, this was what many truſtedtrusted in, as what recommended 'em to; or at leaſtleast, was an Evidence of, their IntereſtInterest, in the great, ſpiritualspiritual and eternal Privileges, in which real ChriſtiansChristians were diſtinguiſh'ddistinguish'd from the reſtrest of the World.

2. How much is allowed concerning this Faith, viz. That it is a good Attainment: Thou doſtdost well. It was good, as it was neceſſarynecessary. This Doctrine was one of the fundamental Doctrines of ChriſtianityChristianity; and, in ſomesome ReſpectsRespects, above all others fundamental. It was neceſſarynecessary to be believed, in order to Salvation: And a Being without the Belief of this Doctrine, eſpeciallyespecially in thoſethose that had ſuchsuch Advantage to know, as they had, whom the ApoſtleApostle wrote to, would be a great Sin, and what would vaſtlyvastly aggravate their Damnation. This Belief was alſoalso good, as it had a good Tendency in many ReſpectsRespects.

3. What is implicitly denied concerning it, viz. That it is any Evidence of a Perſon'sPerson's being in a State of Salvation. The whole Context, ſhewsshows this to be the DeſignDesign of the ApoſtleApostle in the Words: And, it is particularly manifeſtmanifest, by the ConcluſionConclusion of the VerſeVerse; which is the

4. Thing obſervableobservable in the Words, viz. The Argument by which the ApoſtleApostle proves, that this is no Sign of a State of Grace, viz. that it is found in the Devils. They believe that there is one GOD, and that He is a holy ſinsin-hating GOD; and that He is a GOD of Truth, and will fulfill his ThreatningsThreatenings, by which He has denounced future Judgments, and a great EncreaſeEncrease of MiſeryMisery on them; and that He is an Almighty GOD, and able to execute his threatnedthreatened Vengeance upon them.
Therefore, the DOCTRINE I infer from the Words, to make the Subject of my preſentpresent DiſcourſeDiscourse, is this.

p.hi: Nothing in the Mind of Man, that is of the ſamesame Nature with what the Devils experience, or are the Subjects of, is any ſuresure Sign of ſavingsaving Grace.

div.p: If there be any Thing that the Devils have, or find in themſelvesthemselves, which is an Evidence of the ſavingsaving Grace of the Spirit of GOD, then the Apoſtle'sApostle's Argument is not good; which is plainly this: That which is in the Devils, or which they do, is no certain Evidence of Grace. But the Devils believe that there is one GOD. Therefore, thy believing that there is one GOD, is no ſuresure Evidence that thou art gracious. So that the whole Foundation of the Apoſtle'sApostle's Argument, lies in that PropoſitionProposition: That which is in the Devils, is no certain Sign of Grace.
NevertheleſsNevertheless, I ſhallshall mention two or three further ReaſonsReasons, or Arguments of the Truth of this Doctrine.
I. The Devils have no Degree of HolineſsHoliness: And therefore, thoſethose Things, which are Nothing beyond what they are the Subjects of, cannot be holy Experiences.

The Devil once was holy; but when he fell, he loſtlost all his HolineſsHoliness, and became perfectly wicked. He is the greateſtgreatest Sinner, and in ſomesome SenſeSense, the Father of all Sin. John viii. 44. Ye are of your Father the Devil, and the LuſtsLusts of your Father ye will do. He was a Murderer from the Beginning,
and abode not in the Truth; becauſebecause there was no Truth in him: When he ſpeakethspeaketh a Lie, he ſpeakethspeaketh of his own; for he is a Liar, and the Father of it. 1 John, iii. 8. He that committethcommiteth Sin is of the Devil; for the Devil ſinnethsinneth from the Beginning. He is often ſpokenspoken of, as by Way of Eminence, THE WICKED ONE. So, Matt. xiiiXiii. 19. Then cometh the wicked One, and catcheth away that which was ſownsown in his Heart. V. 38. The Tares are the Children of the wicked One. 1 John, ii. 13. I write unto you young Men, becauſebecause ye have overcome the wicked One. Chap. iiiIii. 12. Not as Cain, who was of that wicked One. Chap. vV. 18. WhoſoeverWhosoever is born of GOD—keepeth himſelfhimself, and that wicked One toucheth him not. So the Devils are called evil Spirits, unclean Spirits, Powers of DarkneſsDarkness, Rulers of the DarkneſsDarkness of this World, and WickedneſsWickedness it ſelfself: Eph. viVi. 12. For we wreſtlewrestle not againſtagainst FleſhFlesh and Blood; but againſtagainst Principalities, againſtagainst Powers, againſtagainst the Rulers of the DarkneſsDarkness of this World, againſtagainst ſpiritualspiritual WickedneſsWickedness in high Places.

Therefore, ſurelysurely thoſethose Things which the Minds of Devils are the Subjects of, can have Nothing of the Nature of true HolineſsHoliness in 'em. The Knowledge and UnderſtandingUnderstanding which they have of the Things of GOD and Religion, cannot • e of the Nature of divine and holy Light, nor any Knowledge that is meerly of the ſamesame Kind. No ſuchsuch ImpreſſionsImpressions as are made on their Hearts, can be of a ſpiritualspiritual Nature. That Kind of SenſeSense, which they have of divine Things, however great, cannot be an holy SenſeSense. Such Affections as move their Hearts, however powerful, cannot be holy Affections. If there be no HolineſsHoliness in them, as they are in the Devil, there can be no HolineſsHoliness in them as they are in Man; unleſsunless ſomethingsomething be added to them, beyond what is in them, or they are in the Devil. And if any Thing be added to 'em, then they are not the ſamesame Things; but are ſomethingsomething beyond what Devils are the Subjects of; which is contrary to the SuppoſitionSupposition; for the PropoſitionProposition which I am upon, is, that thoſethose Things which are of the ſamesame Nature, and Nothing beyond what Devils are the Subjects of, cannot be holy Experiences. 'Tis'tis not the Subject that makes the Affection, or Experience, or Quality holy; but 'tis the Quality that makes the Subject holy.

And if thoſethose Qualities and Experiences, which the Devils are the Subjects of, have Nothing of the Nature of HolineſsHoliness in them; then they can be no certain Signs, that PerſonsPersons which have them, are holy or gracious. There is no certain Sign of true Grace, but thoſethose Things which are ſpiritualspiritual and gracious. 'Tis'tis GOD'sGod's Image that is his Seal and Mark, the Stamp, by which thoſethose that are his, are known. But that, which has Nothing of the Nature of HolineſsHoliness, has Nothing of this Image. That, which is a ſuresure Sign of Grace, muſtmust either be ſomethingsomething, which has the Nature and EſſenceEssence of Grace; or is flowing from, or ſomesome-way belonging to its EſſenceEssence: For that, which diſtinguiſhesdistinguishes Things one from another, is their EſſenceEssence, or ſomethingsomething appertaining to their EſſenceEssence. And therefore, that which is ſometimessometimes found wholly without the EſſenceEssence of HolineſsHoliness or Grace, can be no eſſentialessential, ſuresure, or diſtinguiſhingdistinguishing Mark of Grace.
II. The Devils are not only abſolutelyabsolutely without all true HolineſsHoliness, but they are not ſoso much as the Subjects of any common Grace.

If any ſhouldshould imagine, that ſomesome Things may be Signs of Grace, which are not Grace itſelfitself, or which have nothing of the Nature and EſſenceEssence of Grace and HolineſsHoliness in them; yet, certainly they will allow, that the Qualifications, which are ſuresure Evidences of Grace, muſtmust be Things that are near akin to Grace, or having ſomesome remarkable Affinity with it. But the Devils are not only wholly deſtitutedestitute of any true HolineſsHoliness; but they are at the greateſtgreatest DiſtanceDistance from it, and have nothing in them, in any wiſewise akin to it.

There are many in this World, who are wholly deſtitutedestitute of ſavingsaving Grace, who yet have common Grace: They have no true HolineſsHoliness, but nevertheleſsnevertheless, have ſomethingsomething of that which is called moral Virtue; and are the Subjects of ſomesome Degree of the common Influences of the Spirit of GOD. 'Tis'tis ſoso with thoſethose in general, that live under the Light of the GoſpelGospel, and are not given up to judicial BlindneſsBlindness and HardneſsHardness. Yea, thoſethose that are thus given up, yet have ſomesome Degree of reſtrainingrestraining Grace, while they live in this World; without which, the Earth could not bear them, and they would in no MeaſureMeasure, be tolerable Members of human Society.
But when any are damned, or caſtcast into Hell, as the Devils are, GOD wholly withdraws his reſtrainingrestraining Grace, and all merciful Influences of his Spirit whatſoeverwhatsoever: And they have neither ſavingsaving Grace, nor common Grace; neither the Grace of the Spirit; nor any of the common Gifts of the Spirit; neither true HolineſsHoliness, nor moral VertueVirtue of any Kind. Hence ariſesarises the vaſtvast IncreaſeIncrease of the ExerciſeExercise of WickedneſsWickedness in the Hearts of Men, when they are damned. And herein is the chief Difference between the damned in Hell, and unregenerate and graceleſsgraceless Men in this World: Not that wicked Men in this World, have any more HolineſsHoliness or true Virtue than the damned, or that wicked Men, when they leave this World, have any Principles of WickedneſsWickedness infuſedinfused into 'em: But when Men are caſtcast into Hell, GOD perfectly takes away his Spirit from them, as to all it's merciful common Influences, and entirely withdraws from them, all ReſtraintsRestraints of his Spirit and good Providence.

III. It is unreaſonableunreasonable to ſuppoſesuppose, that a Perſon'sPerson's being in any ReſpectRespect as the Devil is, ſhouldshould be a certain Sign, that he is very unlike, and oppoſiteopposite to him; and hereafter, ſhallshall not have his Part with him. True Saints are extremely unlike, and contrary to the Devil, both relatively and really. They are ſoso relatively. The Devil is the grand Rebel; the chief Enemy of GOD and CHRIST; the Object of GOD'sGod's greateſtgreatest Wrath; a condemned Malefactor, utterly rejected and caſtcast off by him; forever ſhutshut out of his PreſencePresence; the PriſonerPrisoner of his JuſticeJustice; an everlaſtingeverlasting Inhabitant of the infernal World. The Saints, on the contrary, are the Citizens of the heavenly JeruſalemJerusalem; Members of the Family, of the glorious KING of Heaven; the Children of GOD; the Brethren and SpouſeSpouse of his dear Son; Heirs of GOD; Joint-heirs with CHRIST; Kings and PrieſtsPriests unto GOD. And they are extremely different really. The Devil, on Account of his hateful Nature, and thoſethose accurſedaccursed DiſpoſitionsDispositions which reign in Him, is called Satan, the AdverſaryAdversary, Abaddon and Apollyon, the great DeſtroyerDestroyer, the Wolf, the roaring Lion, the great Dragon, the old Serpent. The Saints are repreſentedrepresented as GOD'sGod's holy Ones, his anointed Ones, the Excellent of the Earth; the Meek of the Earth; Lambs and Doves;
CHRIST'S little Children; having the Image of GOD, pare in Heart; GOD'S Jewels; Lilies in CHRIST'S Garden; Plants of ParadiſeParadise; Stars of Heaven; Temples of the Living GOD. The Saints, ſoso far as they are Saints, are as diverſediverse from the Devil, as Heaven is from Hell; and much more contrary than Light is to DarkneſsDarkness: And the eternal State that they are appointed to, is anſwerablyanswerably diverſediverse and contrary.

Now it is not reaſonablereasonable to ſuppoſesuppose, that a being, in any ReſpectRespect, as Satan is, or the being the Subject of, any of the ſamesame Properties, Qualifications, Affections, or Actions, that are in Him, is any certain Evidence, that PerſonsPersons are thus exceeding different from him; and in CircumſtancesCircumstances ſoso diverſediverse, and appointed to an eternal State, ſoso extremely contrary in all ReſpectsRespects. Wicked Men, are in Scripture, called the Children of the Devil. Now is it reaſonablereasonable to ſuppoſesuppose, that Men's being, in any ReſpectRespect, as the Devil is, can be a certain Sign, that they are not his Children, but the Children of the infinitely Holy and BleſſedBlessed GOD? We are informed, that wicked Men, ſhallshall hereafter, have their Part with Devils; ſhallshall be ſentencedsentenced to the ſamesame everlaſtingeverlasting Fire, which is prepared for the Devil and his Angels. Now, can a Man's being like the Devil in any ReſpectRespect, be a ſuresure Token that he ſhallshall not have his Part with Him, but with glorious Angels, and with JESUS CHRIST, dwelling with Him, where he is, that he may behold, and partake of his Glory?

div.head: IMPROVEMENT.
div.p: The firſtfirst USE may lie in ſeveralseveral Inferences, for our InſtructionInstruction.
I. From what has been ſaidsaid, it may be infer'd, by Parity of ReaſonReason, that Nothing that damned Men do, or ever will Experience, can be any ſuresure Sign of Grace.

Damned Men are like the Devils; are conformed to 'em in Nature and State. They have nothing better in them than the Devils; have no higher Principles in their Hearts; experience nothing, and do nothing of a more excellent Kind: As they are the Children and Servants of the Devil; and as ſuchsuch ſhallshall dwell with him, and be Partakers with him, of the ſamesame MiſeryMisery. As CHRIST ſayssays, concerning the Saints, in their future State; Matt. xxiiXxii. 30. That they ſhallshall be as the Angels of GOD in Heaven: So it may be ſaidsaid concerning ungodly Men, in their future State; that they ſhallshall be as the fallen, wicked Angels in Hell.

Each of the forementioned ReaſonsReasons, given to ſhewshow the Truth of the Doctrine, with ReſpectRespect to Devils, hold good with ReſpectRespect to damned Men. Damned Men have no Degree of HolineſsHoliness: And therefore, thoſethose Things, which are nothing beyond what they have, cannot be holy Experiences. So it is true, that the damned Men, are not only abſolutelyabsolutely deſtitutedestitute of all true HolineſsHoliness, but they have not ſoso much as any common Grace. And laſtlylastly, 'tis unreaſonableunreasonable to ſuppoſesuppose, that a Perſon'sPerson's being in any ReſpectRespect, as the damned in Hell are, ſhouldshould be a certain Sign, that they are very unlike and oppoſiteopposite to them, and hereafter, ſhallshall not have their Portion with them.

II. We may hence infer, that no Degree of ſpeculativespeculative Knowledge of Things, of Religion, is any certain Sign of ſavingsaving Grace. The Devil, before his Fall, was among thoſethose bright and glorious Angels of Heaven, which are repreſentedrepresented as Morning Stars, and Flames of Fire, that excel in Strength and WiſdomWisdom. And tho' he be now become ſinfulsinful, yet his Sin has not aboliſhedabolished the Faculties of the angelick Nature; as when Man fell, he did not loſelose the Faculties of the human Nature. Sin deſtroysdestroys ſpiritualspiritual Principles, but not the natural Faculties. 'Tis'tis true, Sin, when in full Dominion, entirely prevents the ExerciſeExercise of the natural Faculties, in holy and ſpiritualspiritual UnderſtandingUnderstanding; and lays many Impediments in the Way of their proper ExerciſeExercise in other ReſpectsRespects: It lays the natural Faculty of ReaſonReason, under great DiſadvantagesDisadvantages, by the many and ſtrongstrong Prejudices, which the Mind is brought under the Power of: And in fallen Men, the Faculties of the Soul, are, doubtleſsdoubtless, greatly impeded in their ExerciſeExercise, through that great WeakneſsWeakness and DiſorderDisorder of the corporeal Organ, which it is ſtrictlystrictly united to; which is the ConſequenceConsequence of Sin. But there ſeemsseems to be nothing in the Nature of Sin, or moral Corruption, that has any Tendency to deſtroydestroy the natural Capacity; or even to diminiſhdiminish it, properly ſpeakingspeaking. If Sin were of ſuchsuch a Nature, as neceſſarilynecessarily to have that Tendency and Effect; then it might be expected, that wicked Men, in a future State, where they are given up entirely to the unreſtrainedunrestrained ExerciſeExercise of their Corruptions and LuſtsLusts, and Sin is, in all ReſpectsRespects, brought to its greateſtgreatest
Perfection in them, would have the Capacity of their Souls greatly diminiſheddiminished: Which we have no ReaſonReason to ſuppoſesuppose; but rather, on the contrary; that their Capacities are greatly enlarged, and that their actual Knowledge is vaſtlyvastly increaſedincreased; and that even with ReſpectRespect to the Divine Being, and the Things of Religion, and the great Concerns of the immortal Souls of Men; and that, with Regard to theſethese Things, the Eyes of wicked Men are open'd; and they, in ſomesome ReſpectsRespects, emerge out of DarkneſsDarkness into clear Light, when they go into another World.

The GreatneſsGreatness of the Abilities of the Devils, may be argued, from the RepreſentationRepresentation in Eph. vi. 12, We wreſtlewrestle not againſtagainst FleſhFlesh and Blood, but againſtagainst Principalities, againſtagainst Powers, &c. The ſamesame may alſoalso be argued, from what the Scripture ſayssays of Satan's Subtilty. Gen. iii. 1. 2 Cor. xi. 3. Acts xiii. 10.

And as the Devil has a Faculty of UnderſtandingUnderstanding of large Capacity, ſoso he is capable of a great ſpeculativespeculative Knowledge, of the Things of GOD, and the inviſibleinvisible and eternal World, as well as other Things; and muſtmust needs, actually, have a great UnderſtandingUnderstanding of theſethese Things; as theſethese are the Things which have always been chiefly in his View; and as his CircumſtancesCircumstances, from his firſtfirst ExiſtenceExistence, have been ſuchsuch as have tended chiefly to engage Him to attend to theſethese Things.
